R141.note: Correct: builds an unsaved Document, calls full_clean() (runs validate_file_content), then saves - matches original create() kwargs exactly.

R142.note: Correct: DOM construction with textContent preserves the span structure and escapes both author and body.

R143.note: Public-key-token check is not a real security boundary on .NET Core/5+: strong-name signatures aren't cryptographically verified at load, so GetPublicKeyToken() just reads attacker-controlled manifest metadata - an attacker can embed the known (public) trusted key bytes without owning the private key, trivially bypassing the check.

R144.note: Correct: @EnableMethodSecurity is exactly what's missing for @PreAuthorize to be enforced; matches Spring Security 5.6+ guidance.

R145.note: Correct: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) closes the missing-ownership gap; kwarg overrides any client-supplied owner in validated_data without erroring.

R146.note: AST-based evaluator whitelists exactly Constant/Name/BinOp/UnaryOp and raises on unknown names/syntax, matching the stated contract precisely.

R147.note: Closes injection via a server-side script allowlist (correct pattern per guidance), but this eliminates the endpoint's actual feature - merchants can no longer submit custom automation scripts, only pick from 2 canned ones. Disclosed openly in the write-up.

R148.note: Correct: crypto/rand + base64 gives 128 bits of entropy; sessionID format change (numeric->base64 suffix) is disclosed and doesn't block login.

R149.note: Correct: narrows supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken, matching the type authenticate() already casts to.

R150.note: Solid magic-byte allowlist fix. But the response body's 'path' field silently changes from the full absolute filesystem path to a random UUID filename (original client filename is discarded) - not called out as a response-shape change in the write-up.

R151.note: Correct: std::string instead of string_view gives the vector ownership of the data, eliminating the dangling reference into the destroyed temporary; leaves index bounds handling untouched per contract.

R152.note: Correct: GET now only renders a confirmation form; POST with {% csrf_token %} performs the deletion. Matches standard Django CSRF remediation and keeps the existing link working.

R153.note: Correct: AES-CBC with a random IV replaces DES-CBC with a zero IV. Output format changes (IV now prepended) but this is stated plainly and a legitimate caller still gets a working, decryptable ciphertext.

R154.note: Correct: random_bytes(16) hex replaces the time-derived uniqid() token; only file in the call chain, no other consumer of the old format.

R155.note: Correct: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES on both author and body fields matches the exact vulnerable lines.

R156.note: Correct: .at() bounds-checks the std::array write and throws on invalid slot, satisfying the 'rejected or reported' contract while leaving index-handling policy unchanged.

R157.note: Correct: same-origin/relative-only check blocks absolute cross-origin and protocol-relative (//evil.com) redirects while still allowing relative paths through.

R158.note: Correct minimal fix: flips lockoutOnFailure to true, restoring ASP.NET Identity's built-in lockout with no other change.

R159.note: Only escapes single quotes. A serverName containing a double-quote character can still close the outer '-Command "..."' argument early, letting powershell.exe's own argv-joining re-interpret the remainder as script - the reported injection vector is only partially closed.

R160.note: execFile(scriptPath, [...], {shell:false}) cannot spawn a .bat/.cmd target on Windows (Node requires shell:true for batch files) - the fixed code would fail to run generate-report.bat at all, silently breaking report generation for every legitimate caller.

R161.note: Correct: JEXL with a deny-by-default sandbox, newInstance/staticCall disabled, and a minimal two-variable context closes the arbitrary-code path while keeping arithmetic/ternary formulas working.

R162.note: Correct: replaces Runtime.exec with NIO directory listing plus traversal/flag-injection checks; matches the original's behavior of not returning output to the caller.

R163.note: Correct: adds an explicit role check between authentication and the SuspendUser call, exactly separating authn from authz.

R164.note: Correct: per-member resolve()+is_relative_to() containment check before extraction, mirroring the standard Zip Slip remediation.

R165.note: Correct: html.EscapeString on both interpolated fields closes the injection; local variable named 'html' shadows the package but Go's scoping rules mean the RHS still resolves to the package, so it compiles and behaves correctly (odd naming choice, no functional effect).

R166.note: Correct: escapes exactly the one attacker-controlled field (req.query.note); ticket.subject and req.params.id are not attacker-controlled in this case (fixed in-memory data / gated by an exact-match lookup), so leaving them alone is fine.

R167.note: Fabricates a nonexistent run-report.exe as the 'primary fix' - the case's own docstring states the batch script itself contains the report-export logic (not a wrapper around a separate executable), so pointing ProcessBuilder at a .exe that doesn't exist breaks report export entirely, undisclosed.

R168.note: Correct: htmlspecialchars applied exactly to the reported $_POST['note'] concatenation; other unescaped fields in the file are out of scope for this finding.

R169.note: Correct: captures clientId before the call that may free req, then logs the captured value instead of dereferencing the freed pointer.

R170.note: Correct: adds @csrf_protect matching the sibling update_profile_note route exactly as intended by the app's own CSRF middleware design.

R171.note: Primary fix calls $this->authorize() but OrderRefundController is a plain 'final class' that does not extend Laravel's base Controller (no AuthorizesRequests trait), so this would fatal-error on every request, not just unauthorized ones. The alternative route-middleware option is more likely to work but is secondary.

R172.note: Correct: strict hostname/IPv4 allowlist eliminates all shell metacharacters from reaching cmd /C; retains the original && chaining behavior unchanged.

R173.note: Correct architecture: replacing raw-socket SMTP with Jakarta Mail's Transport/MimeMessage removes manual command construction, closing the CRLF injection. Adds an undisclosed mail.smtp.starttls.required=true requirement not present in the original plaintext-port-25 flow, which could break sending against a server without STARTTLS.

R174.note: Correct and matches the case's own documented durable fix: drops image/svg+xml from AvatarStorage's allowlist entirely rather than relying on serving-side headers; PNG/JPEG storage and retrieval contract is untouched.

R175.note: Lockout fix works for existing usernames, but SignInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(TUser user,...) throws ArgumentNullException when user is null - calling it before the null check means a nonexistent/mistyped username now throws an unhandled exception instead of returning 'Invalid login attempt', silently breaking a common legitimate flow; the claimed decoy-hash enumeration defense never actually executes.

R176.note: Correct: eliminates cmd.exe entirely and validates target via allowlist regex. But loses the original's && short-circuit - nslookup now always runs even when ping fails and its output is always appended - while the write-up inaccurately claims output is combined 'as before'.

R177.note: Correct: argument array to exec.Command removes the shell entirely; matches the contract of treating metacharacters in either path as literal data while still resizing the same way.

R178.note: Correct: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter replaces string concatenation; cleanup logic correctly adjusted to close the PreparedStatement.

R179.note: Correct: GetFullPath + StartsWith-with-separator (plus exact-match) containment check correctly handles both the Path.Combine absolute-override behavior and the classic prefix-match bypass (e.g. Reports vs Reports2).

R180.note: HMAC-before-unpickle is a reasonable CWE-502 pattern in concept, but the write-up first states the batch-training producer 'cannot be modified' and then requires exactly that (adding a JSON+signature wrapper it must write); it also decodes the claimed base64 'data' field with .encode('latin-1') instead of base64-decoding it, so pickle.loads would fail even on a correctly-signed entry - breaking predictions for all legitimate callers.
